action: Take RDM refrigeration controllers off the public internet and apply RDM's new firmware, as Pen Test Partners advises; see RDM advisory RDM-SA-2026-001.
exec: Exposed refrigeration controllers are a risk for supermarkets and cold chain operators, so check whether yours are reachable from the internet.
plain: A flaw in RDM refrigeration controllers led the UK's NCSC to alert supermarkets; RDM released new firmware, but smaller cold chain operators may still be exposed.

key_findings: Pen Test Partners says Danfoss controllers are not particularly popular in the UK and the more popular controllers there are from RDM.
Pen Test Partners says it is not publishing exploits or the discovery method.
RDM has released new firmware, per Pen Test Partners.
recommendations: Take controllers off the public internet.

summary: Pen Test Partners says a significant vulnerability in RDM refrigeration controllers, found by Omega Solutions, led NCSC to issue an urgent alert to UK supermarkets; it calls the issue largely mitigated, though smaller cold chain operators may still be exposed. Cooling Post reports RDM released new firmware. An NCSC spokesperson, quoted by Gulf Daily News, said it immediately took steps to alert and support a small number of UK organisations that may have been affected.
title: UK agencies and Pen Test Partners work to secure exposed RDM supermarket refrigeration controllers

validation.note: Pen Test Partners (read in full) and Gulf Daily News (22 Nov, unbylined, quotes an NCSC spokesperson and Pen Test Partners) each state that a UK operation with NCSC secured vulnerable commercial refrigeration systems. RDM by name and the firmware come from Pen Test Partners and Cooling Post only (near-identical wording, one account). Security.NL relays the BBC, which could not be loaded.
